Rameshchandra vs Ganpat on 31 March, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:8421
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 31 st Of March, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 4656 of 2023
 Rameshchandra
 Versus
 Ganpat And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for the respondent [R-3].
 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant assailing the impugned award dated 30.01.2023 passed by learned 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 223/2019 whereby an amount of Rs.3,35,289/- along with interest has been awarded to the appellant/injured.

entities.text: 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the income of the appellant/injured has been assessed as Rs.5000/- which is on the lower side, whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident i.e. 22.08.2019 is Rs.7700/-.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further submits that nothing has been awarded in the head of permanent disability and even in other heads, the meager amount has been awarded.

Looking to the age of the appellant on the date of the incident i.e.49 years, 25% of the income will be added in the head of future prospects and permanent disability which was proved by the certificate Ex.P/265 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8421 2 MA-4656-2023 issued by Medical Board is 70% and injured has suffered fracture in the backbone and his both legs have been paralysed.

The aforesaid permanent disability has also been proved by Dr. Arvind Gupta (AW-3), whereas learned Claims Tribunal has concluded that it is 23% permanent disability, but in computing the award amount that has not been taken into consideration.
He further submits that in the head of loss of amenities of life, Rs.75,000/- should have been awarded which has not given.
On these submissions, he prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.

3. Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that learned Claims Tribunal has taken due care of all the parameters for assessing just and proper compensation, therefore, no interference is required by allowing this appeal, hence prays Rameshchandra vs Ganpat on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45676400/
1 for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
4 . In light of the aforesaid, where the income of the injured is taken on guess work, Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.
Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on 22.08.2019, income of the appellant/injured is to be taken as Rs.7700/- considering him as 'Unskilled Labour'.

Looking to the age of the appellant/injured, in the head of future prospects, 25%
is to be added.

As per the medical certificate which was proved by Dr. Arvind Gupta (AW-3) and looking to the nature of job of the appellant, permanent disability is taken as 45% and in the head of loss of amenities of life, Rs.75,000/- is to be awarded.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8421 3 MA-4656-2023 Rs.6,75,675/-
Permanent Disability:
(Rs.7700 + 25% FP x 45% PD x 12 x 13) Pain and Suffering: Rs.20,000/-
 Mental pain: Rs.4,000/-
 for special diet: Rs.2,000/-
 for attendant and conveyance: Rs.2,000/-
 for loss of one month's income: Rs.7,700/-
 For loss of amenities of life Rs.75,000/-
For medical bills Rs.3,02,289/-

Total: Rs.10,88,664/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.3,35,289/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.7,53,375/-
5 .
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.10,88,664/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,35,289/-.

Accordingly,
the appellant/injured is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.7,53,375/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The appeal is properly valued and, therefore, no further court fees is required.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate, which was fixed in the impugned award and the other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
6. Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off in above terms.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE soumya Rameshchandra vs Ganpat on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45676400/
